scope: Engine, CPU and controlled DOM; all Lucas commands explicitly simulation. No new Capcom timecode, 1:1 clip or final character art.

checks.name: Only human Lucas changes; all other 345 combat definitions and art are preserved
Ten actions are classified as simulation, with human/mutated variants strictly separate
All ten commands still activate through startup with resources paid exactly once
Remote placement causes no immediate damage and arms only after its stated delay
Manual detonation triggers the owned armed charge once, not poison or healing
An empty detonator gives an explicit message with no resource cost or artificial blast
Detonation before arming neither consumes nor explodes a charge
Remote activation cannot trigger another owner or a non-remote device
The fourth charge retires the oldest instead of exceeding the global capacity
Super creates three visible charges, then three distinct timed blasts
A super shares the same three-object budget with the previously deployed network
Wire catches a fast low crossing in either direction without a skipped contact
A jump over a wire is allowed; landing within its zone can trigger it
Proximity crate waits for arming and explodes only at nearby ground contact
Enemy melee can destroy a remote charge before the activation command
Interrupted setup never spawns a device and never refunds the committed cost
Owner KO, round transition and reset clear the deployed network
Remote charges expire without an explosion, and no future round inherits them
Thrown charge is a timed projectile and detonates once, not a melee strike
Ten deterministic CPU trials finish and the replay reconstructs each exact state
Laboratory explicitly primes a remote fixture for the detonator, with no progression writes
Device cues render without changing objects, input state or resources
